before.supportingExcerpt: The terminal duct lobular unit contains a terminal duct and its associated acini. Acini make milk during lactation; ducts carry it towards the nipple. Lobules and larger lobes are different levels of organisation. Their size and abundance vary with physiology and life stage; an illustrative branch count is not a fixed anatomical count. A schematic grouping bracket is an annotation, not a tissue capsule or basement membrane. NCI DCEG describes TDLU involution with physiological ageing and completion of childbearing as reductions in acini per unit and total unit counts. This is an observational normal-tissue description, not a diagnostic rule for an individual.
before.explanation: The normal terminal duct/lobules, lumen/luminal layer, living myoepithelium, extracellular basement membrane and surrounding stroma are explicit. before.supportingExcerpt: The terminal duct lobular unit contains a terminal duct and its associated acini. Acini make milk during lactation; ducts carry it towards the nipple. Lobules and larger lobes are different levels of organisation. Their size and abundance vary with physiology and life stage; an illustrative branch count is not a fixed anatomical count. A schematic grouping bracket is an annotation, not a tissue capsule or basement membrane. NCI DCEG describes TDLU involution with physiological ageing and completion of childbearing as reductions in acini per unit and total unit counts. This is an observational normal-tissue description, not a diagnostic rule for an individual.

before.supportingExcerpt: The terminal duct lobular unit contains a terminal duct and its associated acini. Acini make milk during lactation; ducts carry it towards the nipple. A schematic grouping bracket is an annotation, not a tissue capsule or basement membrane. NCI DCEG describes TDLU involution with physiological ageing and completion of childbearing as reductions in acini per unit and total unit counts. This is an observational normal-tissue description, not a diagnostic rule for an individual.

points.requirement: An in-situ component within an intact duct boundary can coexist with a separate invasive component in surrounding stroma at one time; no inevitable transition or hole in this particular intact duct is asserted.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Ductal carcinoma in situ describes malignant epithelial cells within the ductal tissue boundary, without invasion identified in that component. An invasive component can coexist in the same specimen. Reading DCIS present does not cancel a separately reported invasive diagnosis. DCIS may be called precancer, noninvasive breast cancer or stage 0 disease; these terms retain the anatomical distinction and do not guarantee that every lesion has the same future risk.
evidence.explanation: The preserved DCIS notes explicitly allow a separately identified invasive component in the same specimen. The fresh image view confirms that the illustrated intact duct and separate stromal cluster are simultaneous spatial components. No transition from that duct is inferred. points.requirement: Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.
evidence.explanation: The living outer cells, extracellular basement membrane and plasma membrane distinction is explicit. UBC normal histology and the Gudjonsson abstract support normal layered organisation, not a universal assay rule. points.requirement: Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.
evidence.explanation: The living outer cells, extracellular basement membrane and plasma membrane distinction is explicit. The new magnification passage states that the illustrated myoepithelial cells are nucleated. UBC normal histology and the Gudjonsson abstract support normal layered organisation, not a universal assay rule. points.requirement: Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. evidence.explanation: The living outer cells, extracellular basement membrane and plasma membrane distinction is explicit. points.requirement: Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.
evidence.explanation: The living outer cells, extracellular basement membrane and plasma membrane distinction is explicit. The new magnification passage states that the illustrated myoepithelial cells are nucleated. UBC normal histology and the Gudjonsson abstract support normal layered organisation, not a universal assay rule. Source scope: {"freshAbstracts":["PMID11801722"],"freshSelectedOfficial":"UBC Cytodiagnosis normal-histology completep22; three selected SEER anatomy blocks.","limit":"Normal-tissue architecture and explicitly invented illustration geometry. No universal cell count, whole textbook/paper or newly verified lineage, density or clinical assertion."}

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Basement membrane beneath an epithelial structure differs from plasma membrane around one cell. Cell polarity describes different inward and outward organisation. Gudjonsson and colleagues' human-cell culture experiments showed that normal myoepithelial cells or laminin-1 could restore luminal orientation in collagen gels; this is model evidence about organisation, not a demonstrated cancer treatment.

points.requirement: Myoepithelial cells are living nucleated cells; the extracellular basement membrane is distinct from those cells and from their plasma membranes.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Typical normal breast ducts and acini have luminal epithelial cells facing the lumen, an outer living myoepithelial layer, extracellular basement membrane and then stroma. Myoepithelial cells have contractile features that help move milk; they are not the chest muscle. Basement membrane contains matrix proteins such as laminins and type IV collagen, not living cells.
